chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, by his chain, raised it from Abu
Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The one who prays two Rak'at with 'Say He is Allah, One' in every Rak'at sixty times, finishes, and there is not a sin between him and Allah.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas sixty times in each Rak'at of a two-Rak'at prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith details the Salat al-Ikhlas, a highly revered voluntary prayer where Surah Al-Ikhlas is recited sixty times per Rak'ah, emphasizing the power of divine unity (Tawhid) for spiritual purification. The phrase 'infatala' (was released/delivered) signifies a complete absolution of sins, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that consistent devotion to this specific recitation serves as a potent means of drawing near to Allah and erasing minor transgressions. This practice is often linked to the broader tradition of night prayers and is considered a significant act of worship for seeking forgiveness and spiritual elevation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, by  his chain, 
(It has been) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who prays four Rak’at of Salāt with [112:1] Say He Allah is One (Chapter 112) sixty times in every Rak’at, would wrap up (finish), and there would not be a sin (remaining) between him and Allahazwj’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from through the chain of his narrators in a marfu’ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the text is the same as the previous Hadith except that it says, ‘Read Chapter 112 of the Holy Quran sixty times in each Rak‘at.’”
